ISSUE32_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.SCOPE: Target-only correction. Historical approved clauses and approval records remain as evidence of prior decisions; incompatible historical API paths are not the target contract. No production implementation authorized.
ISSUE32_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.GOAL: One unified direct/group conversation service exposed solely through the unversioned /conversations HTTP resource tree, authenticated exclusively with BFE Drive Internal Auth validated DPoP-bound sessions.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: All target conversation HTTP operations use /conversations and its unversioned descendants. /v1 and /v2 are not target HTTP APIs. Existing /v2 domain behavior is the implementation migration baseline, not a second API.

Every protected target HTTP request requires DPoP proof bound to the validated BFE Drive session through existing Internal Auth; plain Bearer is not an accepted authentication scheme. WebSocket authentication and subscriptions preserve required independent membership verification and revocation rules.
Direct and group conversations share one conversation identity, message stream, authorization model and history semantics, retaining type-specific membership and ownership rules.

Retain all functional direct/group conversation behavior, permissions, message/document handling and idempotency from the working /v2 implementation. No legacy-client support, production-data inventory or migration is in scope; destructive removal of populated legacy tables is not authorized.

A 1:1 conversation is created by authenticated account UUID and distinct peer UUID. Self-direct is rejected. Creation for the same unordered pair is unique and concurrency-safe. Personal hide affects only caller visibility, never peer access, messages or direct identity.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for direct without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Authenticated user creates named group with owner and selected account UUIDs. Maximum 100 members including owner. Creator is owner. Group supports rename, invited-member changes, role management and departure. A member may leave. The owner must transfer ownership to another current group member before leaving; if there is no other current member, the last owner cannot leave. Exactly one owner must remain after each successful operation.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for group without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Owner may manage group and appoint or dismiss admins, while preserving exactly one owner; admin can only perform explicitly allowed membership or rename operations, cannot remove owner/other admin, appoint admins or transfer ownership; member cannot administer group. BFE Drive ADMIN status does not grant Chat membership or management.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for roles without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Every membership addition/removal creates an auditable bounded visibility interval. Read and message delivery are permitted only for messages within caller intervals. On rejoin, messages from the gap stay hidden. Removal immediately blocks subsequent protected operations and active WebSocket subscriptions. Membership mutations and send/delivery authorization have a defined atomic ordering.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for membership without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Each conversation has one stable monotonic conversation-scoped message order and cursor pagination, default 50 and max 100 messages per page. Every history query filters by authenticated viewer membership intervals. The same visibility rule applies to reconnect and historical catch-up.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for history without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Only authenticated current members send messages; sender identity is never supplied by a trusted client field. Text maximum 16384 UTF-8 bytes, request JSON maximum 65536 bytes. Idempotency key replay returns original result for identical content and 409 Conflict for different content; concurrency cannot create duplicates.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for message without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Optional message context holds document ID and title; preserve both in message history and events. Chat neither copies document content nor grants any BFE Drive document rights. Document access is independently checked by BFE Drive.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for document without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Centrifuge publishes persisted messages only to currently authorized members. Revalidate authorized subscriptions and revocation even for established sockets. Reconnect recovers missed messages through persisted conversation history; multi-device membership and read states remain coherent.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for realtime without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Read marker is monotonically increasing per account and conversation and shared across devices. Unread counts include only authorized messages sent by other users. One member cannot advance another member read marker.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for read without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: All Chat-specific conversation state and ACLs are within bfe_chat. BFE Drive sessions are validated through existing Internal Auth UDS; account UUID alone grants no Chat authorization. Reject out-of-scope access without leaking data.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for isolation without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Group names limited to 256 UTF-8 bytes; no more than 100 group members; JSON body max 65536 bytes; message text max 16384 UTF-8 bytes; history page max 100. Reject invalid input before changes or publications.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for limits without changes to legacy clients or production data.

DRAFT_REALTIME_REVISION.SCOPE: Requirements-only proposal to supersede REQ32-REALTIME's Centrifuge target. ISSUE32 approval provenance remains historical; this proposal is not effective until Human Approval. Technology.xml, DevelopmentPlan.xml and Contracts.xml remain unchanged.

PLATFORM_EVIDENCE.SOURCE: Android Doze suspends network access and defers background work; Android recommends FCM for downstream realtime messaging and high-priority user-visible notifications. A direct ntfy stream must not be treated as guaranteed during Doze.

Android 14+ requires a declared foreground-service type and associated permission. specialUse requires a manifest subtype property and Google Play review; remoteMessaging is limited to its documented text-message continuity use case.
Android 12+ generally prohibits starting a foreground service from the background except documented exemptions; the target flow must start while the app is visible or be justified by an exemption.

For apps targeting Android 15+, dataSync foreground services have a six-hour total limit per 24-hour period while backgrounded, so dataSync is not a suitable assumption for an indefinite subscription stream.

Google Play requires foreground-service use to be core-functionality relevant, user-initiated or user-perceptible, user-stoppable, justified against deferral/interruption, and limited to the necessary duration; Android 14+ service declarations are reviewed.
ntfy supports long-lived HTTP JSON, SSE and WebSocket subscriptions plus bounded cached replay. These transport events and cache are not authoritative BFE message history.
Android 13+ requires runtime POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission for ordinary notifications; users can also disable app notifications or channels.

The ntfy Android app uses a foreground service for its own instant-delivery mode in Doze and displays a persistent service notification. This is evidence about the ntfy app, not proof that a BFE client implementation has equivalent lifecycle behavior or policy approval.
Self-hosted ntfy FCM support requires Firebase configuration and a custom-built Android app. It does not automatically register or securely deliver notifications to an unrelated BFE Android client.
UnifiedPush requires an application connector and a device distributor; the receiving application must handle push messages and its own notification rendering.
On Android, after the user force-quits the app from device settings, it must be manually reopened for FCM messages to start working again.

DRAFT_REALTIME_REVISION.SUPERSEDES_PROPOSAL: Centrifuge is not the proposed target realtime transport; ntfy is proposed instead. AAG_SCENARIOS.ACTOR: A current BFE session user who may access only conversations authorized by backend membership and visibility intervals.
Owns approval of release readiness, compatibility evidence and production boundaries; this draft does not grant deployment authority.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: ntfy replaces Centrifuge as target realtime transport, not an additional channel or source of truth. Centrifuge remains only the current approved baseline until the draft is approved and dependent contracts are revised.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Target requirements do not retain Centrifuge as a parallel channel; HTTP/PostgreSQL remain authoritative for message/history/read-state fetches.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Backend determines recipients and topic mapping from authenticated identity, authoritative membership and bounded visibility intervals. The sender is excluded from recipients. Clients cannot choose recipient lists or arbitrary topics; topic names alone are not authorization. Exact ntfy ACL/auth mechanism is unresolved.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Negative tests prove unauthorized cross-account/conversation subscription and publish are denied; recipients are selected server-side and the message sender receives no ntfy event for their own message.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Member removal, rejoin, visibility change, session revocation and account switch invalidate prior ntfy authorization. Active subscribers must stop receiving protected signals within an approved tested bound; immediate ntfy-side revocation is not assumed. Administrative Chat disablement is separate: an existing subscription may continue receiving only opaque wakeToken, while new Chat operations, history requests and subscriptions are denied; after re-enable, the client catches up through authorized history. This does not add periodic BFE-session checks, session revocation or a Drive callback.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Membership/session revocation stops protected events after the approved bound; rejoin does not reveal gap history; expired/revoked/cross-session capability fails closed. During administrative Chat disablement, an existing subscription may receive only wakeToken and cannot authorize history/API access; new operations/history/subscriptions are denied; re-enable triggers authorized history catch-up.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: ntfy events are wake-up signals only. On initial connection, reconnect, app resume or a suspected gap, coalesce refresh work and fetch authorized history from the HTTP API; PostgreSQL and the API remain authoritative. Dedupe and display order use stable message identity/order returned by authoritative history, never ntfy event IDs, timestamps, delivery order or cached replay. The target history contract MUST provide stable persisted message identity, stable monotonic conversation-scoped order, and server-issued cursor pagination. Current unversioned API conformance is unverified and remains a blocking evidence gate; if it does not conform, a formally approved upstream contract/conformance resolution is required before implementation. A missing, duplicate, delayed or reordered ntfy event must not cause message loss or duplicate display.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Duplicate, missing, reordered and delayed wakeToken events converge to backend-authoritative history/read state without duplicate messages or visibility outside membership intervals. The accepted history contract identifies stable message identity and pagination/cursor semantics; no cursor is inferred from ntfy metadata.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: REQ32-DOCUMENT continues to require document ID and title in authorized backend message history and backend/internal events. The publisher-controlled BFE application data carried in the ntfy message MUST be a JSON object with exactly one application field named wakeToken whose value is opaque and non-identifying. This application payload is distinct from the ntfy transport JSON envelope, which may contain transport metadata such as id, time, event and topic. Envelope metadata is never BFE message identity, ordering, cursor or authorization. Neither application data nor notification text may contain message text, document title/content, conversation ID, message ID, user ID, access tokens, DPoP proofs, private keys or other protected identifiers. wakeToken is only a wake-up signal: it does not identify a conversation, grant authorization or authorize API/history access. Chat membership does not grant Drive document access.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Payload/log inspection confirms the ntfy event contains only wakeToken and no message text, document title/content, conversation/message/user identifiers or credentials; authorized backend history/internal events retain document ID/title as required by REQ32-DOCUMENT; conversation membership cannot bypass Drive ACL checks.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Successful database commit remains a successful send if ntfy publication fails or times out. Retry/outbox/equivalent, dedupe and sanitized observability must be designed and approved; no mechanism is presumed.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Post-commit ntfy outage does not change committed send result; failure is observable without secrets and approved retry/dedupe behavior is testable.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Subscriptions are scoped to current BFE session and membership. Logout/account switch/revocation invalidates old subscriptions; events grant no authority to read messages, and each history request independently uses existing session-bound DPoP HTTP authorization.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: After account switch old subscriptions and state are cleared before new data appears; old-account history is not exposed under the new account.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Conversation membership, realtime topic membership and document access are separate permission domains. Only BFE Drive authorizes document content; Chat does not infer or proxy Drive ACLs.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: A user receiving a conversation signal but lacking Drive permission cannot fetch/open the document.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: This requirements revision does not change bfe-drive, bfe-drive-client production behavior, Drive sessions/ACLs or production infrastructure. Actual chat package integration, compatibility, rollout and rollback must be evidenced before implementation.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Reviewed release plan identifies deployed client versions/dependencies, compatibility, migration/coexistence if required, rollback triggers and release owner; no production changes occur in this phase.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: ntfy supports long-lived HTTP JSON, SSE and WebSocket subscription transports; the exact session-bound authentication and browser CORS contract remain blocking. FCM/Firebase and UnifiedPush are excluded by the current Project Owner constraints and are not target alternatives in this revision. Android system notification rendering belongs to BFE Client and is separate from ntfy app notifications. Background streaming is conditional on the BFE-owned foreground-service candidate in REQ36-RT-11; neither service-type eligibility nor Google Play approval is assumed. No universal background delivery or ntfy-specific BFE DPoP support is assumed.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Transport/auth evidence covers supported browsers and Android lifecycle states; tests distinguish in-app realtime refresh from BFE-owned system notifications, validate stream reconnect and authoritative-history reconciliation, and cover notification permission/channel settings, Doze, process death, service stop/reboot and force-stop. FCM/Firebase and UnifiedPush are not implemented or treated as target alternatives; FGS eligibility remains a blocking evidence gate.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Android system notifications are a separate client-owned behavior, not a notification generated by the separate ntfy Android app. The target candidate preserves the Project Owner's constraints: no FCM/Firebase, no UnifiedPush and no additional user-installed app. The active BFE Android Client consumes the ntfy HTTP JSON/SSE stream and uses every event only as a wake-up hint; the authorized HTTP API and PostgreSQL remain authoritative. For best-effort background delivery, the candidate is a BFE-owned native foreground service started from a visible activity after the user explicitly enables instant notifications. It must immediately enter foreground state with a persistent, accurate, user-stoppable notification and maintain the stream only while the feature is enabled. Android 12+ generally prevents starting an FGS after the app is already backgrounded; a restart after process death or reboot is not assumed. Android 13+ requires runtime POST_NOTIFICATIONS for ordinary BFE notifications and users may disable notification channels. Android 14+ requires the service type and matching permission. dataSync is not suitable for an indefinite stream for Android 15+ targets because of its six-hour-per-24-hour background limit. remoteMessaging is not assumed to cover a server-connected ntfy listener because its documented purpose is text-message transfer/continuity between devices. specialUse is the current conditional candidate only if no other type accurately fits; it requires FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE, android:foregroundServiceType="specialUse", android.app.PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE and Google Play declaration/review. Play eligibility is not confirmed; its policy requires a core user-beneficial use, user awareness/control and justification for uninterrupted duration. Do not request battery-optimization exemption by default. If the FGS type or policy is rejected, the current constraints block dependable background notifications and the issue must return to Project Owner; do not silently substitute FCM/Firebase or UnifiedPush. The ntfy event contains exactly the opaque wakeToken, never message/conversation/user/document identifiers or credentials, and grants no API/history access. Duplicate, missing, delayed or reordered events are harmless refresh hints: clients reconcile through the authorized HTTP history contract specified by REQ36-RT-04. A stable server-issued cursor must be defined there before implementation if the existing unversioned API does not expose one; stable message identity/order comes from authoritative history, never ntfy event ID/time or cached replay. On notification tap, the client MUST resolve the corresponding conversation through a separate backend lookup authenticated by the current BFE session/DPoP, then re-check current session and conversation membership before displaying protected content. wakeToken may be supplied only as an opaque lookup selector; it contains no conversation/user/message identifier and grants no authority. The lookup contract is specified by REQ36-RT-12. Its proposed 30-day lifetime, reusable/non-consuming behavior, and required database uniqueness constraint remain unapproved/blocking until the Project Owner accepts the proposal and the upstream GRACE gates are passed. Delivery is not guaranteed during Doze, network loss, service/process death, reboot, force-stop or disabled notifications. After the client resumes or reconnects, it must reconcile authoritative history using the current session-bound authorization.

ANDROID_NOTIFICATION_MATRIX.STATE: The ntfy stream refreshes the open chat through authorized HTTP history; notification display is separate from the in-app realtime update.
Best-effort BFE-owned notification only while the user-enabled FGS and stream remain active; a persistent service notification and user stop control are required.
No live-stream or notification delivery is promised.
Delivery may continue if the service/connection survives, but Android may suspend network access; no latency guarantee.
Reconnect when possible, then reconcile from authoritative history; absence of a stream event is not proof that no message exists.
Service restart and delivery are not guaranteed; reconcile after manual launch/resume.
Automatic FGS restart is not assumed; reconcile after the user launches/resumes BFE.
No delivery is promised until the user manually launches BFE again; then fetch authoritative history.
No ordinary BFE system notification when POST_NOTIFICATIONS or channel settings prevent display; the OS controls presentation of the required FGS notification.
Stop the old subscription/service and clear prior-session state before using the new session.
An existing subscription may receive only wakeToken; new Chat operations, history requests and subscriptions are denied; after re-enable, perform authorized history catch-up.

REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify that, with notification permission and an eligible user-enabled active service, a received wakeToken produces a generic BFE-owned system notification without the ntfy app. Verify foreground/background, screen-off/Doze, network loss/reconnect, service stop, OS process death, reboot, force-stop, denied POST_NOTIFICATIONS/channel disabled, logout/account switch, and Chat disable/re-enable. Demonstrate service start from a visible activity, persistent notification, user stop, exact declared FGS type/permissions, and Google Play declaration/review evidence before claiming release suitability. No delivery guarantee is claimed for unsupported states; after force-stop, history is reconciled only after manual launch. Notification tap requires current-session authorization; wakeToken itself never authorizes access.

REQUIREMENT.refs: REQ32-AUTH REQ32-MEMBERSHIP REQ32-ISOLATION REQ32-HISTORY REQ36-RT-05 REQ36-RT-11
REQUIREMENT.RULE: Define the target backend notification lookup as POST /conversations/notification-target with Content-Type application/json and body exactly {"wakeToken":"opaque-token"}; query strings are forbidden. The endpoint reuses the existing HTTP boundary: exactly one Authorization: DPoP access-token header and one DPoP proof header, validated by the existing Internal Auth UDS and Validator.ValidateCaller against the exact POST method and public HTTPS path. It never accepts wakeToken as authentication or authorization. The response on success is JSON {"conversationId":"uuid"} only, with Cache-Control: no-store and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; it contains no message ID, message text, title, membership details or other protected content. The backend maps the opaque token to the existing server-side notification attempt record (issue25_publish_attempts.wake_token -> viewer_id, membership_epoch, conversation_id, created_at); the token itself contains no account, conversation or message identifier and is not a capability. The lookup MUST match exactly one stored record, require viewer_id to equal the authenticated caller account, require the record to be unexpired, require the caller's current active membership epoch to equal the recorded membership_epoch, and re-check that the conversation and Chat access are currently available. This check is repeated for every request; cached authorization and client-supplied identity/membership are forbidden. Only conversationId is returned; the client then fetches history through the existing authorized HTTP history endpoint, which applies current membership and visibility-interval rules. The target token lifetime is proposed as 30 days from the server-recorded created_at; expiration is absolute and is not extended by lookup. The lookup is reusable and non-consuming until expiry because it has no authority by itself and every use repeats session/membership checks; repeated taps return the same authorized conversationId and have no side effects. A session revocation/logout must be reflected by existing Internal Auth validation; account switch fails because the authenticated account must match viewer_id. Removal/rejoin revokes old notification routing because the current membership epoch no longer matches the stored epoch. Expired, unknown, malformed, duplicate-mapped, foreign-account, revoked-epoch or unavailable-conversation tokens all return the same non-disclosing 404 NOT_FOUND; invalid/revoked session or DPoP returns existing 401 auth errors; Internal Auth or database unavailability returns 503 without returning routing data. Invalid JSON/token format returns 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. Responses are never cached and wakeToken must not appear in URLs or application logs. The existing schema stores created_at and mapping fields but has no unique constraint on wake_token or explicit expiry column; implementation is blocked until a unique database constraint/index for wake_token and deterministic expiry enforcement are included in an approved downstream contract/migration. This is a requirements proposal only; no endpoint, schema or migration is authorized by this artifact.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: On the exact POST endpoint, a valid current-session DPoP caller with a matching active membership epoch receives only conversationId; the same request repeated before expiry returns the same result without consuming or extending the token. Missing/invalid DPoP, stale/revoked session, wrong account, removed/rejoined membership epoch, expired/unknown token, ambiguous duplicate mapping, unavailable conversation or disabled Chat returns no conversation identifier and reveals no token/conversation existence. After logout/account switch, old session validation fails or the new account fails viewer_id matching. History is fetched separately and remains filtered by current membership visibility intervals. Confirm the unique wake_token database constraint and 30-day created_at-based expiry rule before implementation; neither the current schema nor this draft alone proves them implemented.

DRAFT_REALTIME_REVISION.INVARIANT: ntfy signals never grant access or replace backend authorization/history.
Payloads and diagnostics never disclose protected content or credentials.
A subscription is valid only for its current authenticated session and authorized membership interval.
Chat membership or ntfy topic access never grants Drive document permissions.
Failure of the realtime transport cannot reverse or misreport an already committed message; retries must not create duplicate authoritative messages.
Requirements-only work does not change production repositories, data, permissions, configuration or infrastructure; rollout requires separate evidence and authorization.
BFE Android Client, not the separate ntfy app, owns the BFE system notification. A notification is a best-effort wake-up and never grants access or replaces authorized history.

A wakeToken lookup returns a conversation identifier only after current session/DPoP validation, exact recipient match, unexpired unique mapping and current membership-epoch authorization; wakeToken never grants authority.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Account A attempts to subscribe to a topic or conversation authorized only for account B.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Subscription or publish is denied without disclosing topic contents; a topic name is not authorization.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: A member is removed or rejoins while an old subscription is still connected.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Protected delivery stops within the approved bound; the visibility gap remains hidden after rejoin.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: The user logs out or switches from account A to account B while realtime is active.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: The old subscription and account-scoped cache are cleared before account B data is shown; old-account history is not exposed.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: Realtime events are missing, duplicated, delayed or reordered, followed by reconnect.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: HTTP history/read-state reconciliation converges to backend-authoritative state without duplicate messages or visibility outside membership intervals.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: PostgreSQL commits a message, then ntfy publication times out or is unavailable.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: The send remains successful; failure is observable without secrets; the approved retry/dedupe contract does not create duplicate messages.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: A browser cannot use the chosen subscription auth mechanism, or Android is suspended, killed or force-stopped.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: No credentials are placed in URLs; no unsupported background-delivery guarantee is assumed; the client reconciles authoritative state when it can resume.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: The draft is reviewed while deployed-client integration and rollback compatibility are still unknown.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: Implementation and rollout remain blocked; no production repository, data, permission, configuration or infrastructure changes occur.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: The BFE Android client receives wakeToken while its eligible background subscription/service is active and the user has enabled notifications.
MENTAL_SCENARIO.EXPECTED: The BFE client posts a generic system notification without protected content; the separate ntfy app's notification is not counted as success.

MENTAL_SCENARIO.INPUT: The user force-stops BFE Client, or Android kills the process, and messages arrive during the inactive period.
